GHSA-3m5p-2c4r-xxw2.pat: return function \(a, i\) \{ return i < tp \}
GHSA-3m5p-2c4r-xxw2.hole: A numeric trustProxy setting trusts X-Forwarded-* entries by hop count without checking the immediate peer, so a direct client can add enough forwarded hops to spoof its IP, host and protocol.

GHSA-4g9m-rffv-h6wq.hole: A caller with the shared (non-admin) bearer token gets its owner and org from the x-crabbox-owner and x-crabbox-org request headers, so it can act as any other owner or organization.

GHSA-5gpm-rgj3-9q76.hole: When a request body is chunked or sent over HTTP/2 and is larger than the buffer, the policy check sees only the first part and is never told the body was cut, so a policy that inspects the body can be passed by putting the forbidden content past the limit.

GHSA-6mwv-4mrm-5p3m.hole: The Kiro sign-in flow puts a caller-supplied region straight into the upstream host name (oidc.<region>.amazonaws.com), so a crafted region sends the request, with its credentials, to a host the caller picks.

GHSA-7j4w-x8x8-5mvg.hole: Tarball extraction checks each entry's path by name only and does not resolve symlinks it already created, so an entry under a symlink pointing at .. writes files outside the extraction folder.

GHSA-9q47-3cm2-2rp8.pat: # Get client IP, handling X-Forwarded-For for proxies
also: # Get client IP, safely handling X-Forwarded-For
GHSA-9q47-3cm2-2rp8.hole: The login rate limit, API key checks and sign-in audit log take the client IP from the X-Forwarded-For header any caller can set, so an attacker gets a fresh rate-limit bucket per request and can forge the logged IP.

GHSA-c9w5-qp6m-m395.hole: Token exchange checks the subject token's signature with the requesting application's certificate and never checks the token's audience, so a token from one application or organization can be exchanged for a token of another.

GHSA-f8c7-rwf9-fmgm.hole: A missing comma joins two entries of the blocked-path list, so /api/terminals is not blocked and anyone can open a server shell without signing in.

GHSA-h5gx-45rj-2h5j.hole: The Hub upload sends the private key in a custom header with an HTTP client that follows redirects, and Go only strips standard auth headers on a cross-host redirect, so the key goes to whatever host the Hub URL redirects to.

GHSA-hrw6-wg82-cm62.hole: The static file finder accepts absolute paths and checks they exist before checking they are inside the served folder, so on Windows a request for a UNC path makes the server connect out and hand over the user's password hash.

GHSA-hxpf-9xvq-wph8.hole: Tool arguments from the model are pasted into REST paths, so an id of ../token reaches the token endpoint and skips the tool's API-key redaction, leaking the key to the model.

GHSA-jcxm-m3jx-f287.hole: The unsafe-option guard blocks clone's -u (upload-pack) switch only in its plain form, so combined short flags like -vu or other spellings still pass a command for git to run.

GHSA-m98r-6667-4wq7.hole: Creating a run on a thread never checks that the thread belongs to the caller, so any signed-in user can start runs on another user's thread.

GHSA-mw3h-qjxj-6xg9.hole: The URL signature check strips the signature with str.replace, which removes every copy, so an attacker can put the valid signature elsewhere in a different URL and have it validate.

GHSA-rmxw-pq4x-3fvh.pat: // Validate each path and collect absolute paths; skip any traversal attempts
GHSA-rmxw-pq4x-3fvh.hole: The bulk zip download checks only that each path stays in the web root, not the per-folder .goshs access rules, so files those rules protect or block can be downloaded without credentials.

GHSA-v667-gc2r-2xm7.hole: The guard that blocks re-running first-time setup checks only /api/user/init, while /open/user/init skips sign-in and is rewritten to the same handler, so anyone can reset the admin login.

GHSA-vx32-xf7g-9ghr.hole: Tar extraction checks the target path with a plain string prefix, so an entry like ../context-evil/x (a sibling folder sharing the prefix) is written outside the destination.

GHSA-xgjr-7j9q-2h4r.hole: The subscriber export runs the caller's SQL filter without the table allowlist check the search path applies, so a user allowed to filter by SQL can read any table, including admin password hashes and mail settings.

GHSA-xgm2-5f3f-mvvc.hole: The API Gateway v1 adapter drops a repeated header value when it is a substring of a value already set, so the app sees a different header list than the gateway forwarded.

GHSA-xvq9-wjp8-hwqf.hole: The language and namespace checks allow ':' and '//', so when the load path starts with the placeholder a value like http:127.0.0.1:8080 turns the request URL into one on another host.
